title: FullStack-Agent: Enhancing Agentic Full-Stack Web Coding via Development-Oriented Testing and Repository Back-Translation
one_liner: Build real web apps, not only polished pages, by combining planning, codebase navigation, bug finding, and tests that check the front end, server, and storage together.
lead: This paper targets a gap in code agents for websites. Many systems can draw attractive pages, yet they fail once the task needs form handling, server logic, or saved data. FullStack-Agent treats full-stack coding as a development workflow rather than a one-shot page generation problem. It combines a multi-worker builder, a self-improvement loop built from existing repositories, and a benchmark that checks whether the produced app actually works across the full request path.

problem.h2: Why full-stack coding is harder than page generation
paras: A polished page can hide the absence of real application logic. A user may see forms, tables, and buttons, yet no request reaches a server and no data is saved. That is why front-end-only success is an incomplete measure for web coding agents.

A real web app must coordinate several linked parts: page behavior, server routes, storage, package versions, and bug repair. If one part is wrong, the whole request path fails because the app depends on end-to-end agreement across files and services.

callout.b: The paper's claim in one line.
callout.html: Treat full-stack coding as planning plus testing plus repair, because visible page quality alone does not prove that the application works.

panels.title: 1. A page looks finished
panels.viz_args: forms, charts, and buttons appear correct
panels.caption: A good-looking page can still be empty if no server logic and no storage support it.

panels.title: 2. Real apps span several layers
panels.caption: Page logic, server routes, and storage must all line up because a request crosses each layer in turn.

panels.title: 3. Multi-worker development loop
panels.caption: Different workers focus on different coding tasks so the system can reason over the codebase instead of only producing raw text.

panels.title: 4. Test the whole request path
panels.caption: Development-oriented tests expose whether the app truly works because they exercise the linked path from user action to saved result.

panels.title: 5. Learn from many repositories
panels.caption: Back-translation turns existing projects into training signals, so the builder improves on realistic full-stack patterns.

steps.text: The system first decides which features, routes, and storage pieces are needed so code edits can be judged against an explicit development plan.
Workers inspect existing files and dependencies because correct edits depend on where data already enters, moves, and is stored.
The builder writes code and then isolates likely fault locations, so repair work targets the files that actually break the request path.
The benchmark checks page behavior, server behavior, and storage behavior together because each layer can pass alone while the end-to-end flow still fails.
Back-translation turns existing web projects into training examples because the model then sees realistic project structure and repair patterns.

paras: The paper changes web coding evaluation from page appearance to full application behavior, and it changes training from short synthetic prompts to repository-derived development traces.
object.object: the development loop for full-stack web coding

hidden.name: end-to-end consistency of the application state path
paras: The key hidden quantity is whether the same data idea is represented consistently across page code, server code, and storage code. A button may send one field name while the server expects another, or the server may write a shape that the page cannot later read. Those mismatches stay hidden until a real task crosses the full path.

FullStack-Agent tries to expose that hidden consistency through development-oriented tests. The tests help because they do not stop at surface rendering. They force one user action to travel through each layer, so broken links become visible.

heat.caption: Darker cells mark the hidden agreements that determine whether one user action survives the whole trip through the app.

reads.html: The hidden quantity is whether all app layers mean the same thing when they handle one piece of data, because one mismatch can make the app fail even when each file seems reasonable in isolation.
The system seeks full-stack consistency by coupling repository-aware construction with tests that directly probe front-end, server, and storage behavior.

paras: The main reason this helps is that full-stack errors are often relational errors, because a single file may look correct while still disagreeing with another file about names, routes, or saved fields. A development loop that only inspects local code quality misses those cross-file agreements because they appear only when the pieces interact.

The repository back-translation step helps for a second reason because real projects contain recurring structures for server handlers, saved data, and page updates. Turning repositories back into training examples gives the system many concrete traces of how working projects are organized, so later generation can reuse patterns that already preserve end-to-end agreement.

stages.s: test front end, server, and storage

math.h2: Score an app by linked-layer success
math.words: A simple summary is to reward an app when the same task works on the page, on the server, and in storage, then subtract the cost of failures that break the path between those layers.
symbols: overall value of one generated application
how well the page behavior passes the relevant tests
how well server routes and handlers pass their tests
how well reads and writes pass storage tests
penalty for mismatches that break the full request path

worked.title: A tiny worked example
lines: App A renders the page and accepts form input, so page pass is 8.
Its server route works, so server pass is 8, but it never saves the data, so storage pass is 1.
The missing save path adds a break cost of 5.
App B scores 7 on the page, 7 on the server, and 7 on storage, with break cost 1.
App B wins because slightly lower page polish is worth more when the full path actually works.

math.note: The real system uses richer tests and learning signals, but the paper's point is captured by this score: reward linked-layer success, not isolated page quality.

charts.title: Front-end-focused coding agent
charts.note: The page layer is stronger than the deeper layers because the system is optimized for visible output rather than full application behavior.

charts.title: FullStack-Agent
charts.note: The paper reports gains on all three layers because the builder, the tests, and the repository-derived learning signal are all aligned to full-stack success.

items.b: Tests can still miss realistic failures.
items.html: A benchmark can cover many paths and still miss a deployment-only fault, so passing tests is strong evidence but not a full guarantee.

items.b: Repository back-translation may copy local habits.
items.html: If the source repositories share one narrow style, the training signal may favor that style even when a new task would benefit from a different structure.

items.b: Bug localization may narrow too soon.
items.html: If the system blames the wrong file early, later repair effort can be wasted because the true mismatch lives in another layer of the request path.
The method is strongest when app plans, repository evidence, and end-to-end tests point to the same target behavior, because then each repair step has clearer feedback.

demo.h2: What a runnable demo should prove
paras: Build a small web application task set with at least one create action, one read action, and one update action. For each task, require the app to render a page, hit a server route, and save or load data from storage. Log where failures occur: page, route, or storage. Compare a front-end-heavy agent against a development-oriented full-stack agent.

The demo should show higher end-to-end pass rates for the full-stack agent because tests expose broken links across layers and repository-based learning gives the builder better examples of working project structure. The logs should also show shorter repair cycles when bug localization points to the correct layer.
demo.closing: A convincing demo must prove that full-stack coding improves when the agent is trained and evaluated on full request paths, because page appearance alone does not measure application correctness.
